label: UNSEEN_VINTAGE_REVERSAL
method: Complete reporting of the frozen unseen-vintage comparison. Nothing fitted, nothing changed.

populations.duration_and_encoding_note: Unseen vintages 2018, 2020 and 2022 receive the frozen zero-reference cohort encoding because they are unrepresented in development, and their duration support differs from the seen vintages. The frozen artifacts do not publish a duration-band distribution for this population.

primary_decision_metric.metric: M2-M1 paired temporal joint log loss, smaller better
primary_decision_metric.statement: On the protocol's own primary decision metric the unseen-vintage population reverses sign: M2 is better than M1 by 0.000819, against being worse by 0.016122 on the seen-vintage population, with 2.62x the intervals and 3.09x the facilities.

calibration_finding: The payoff calibration direction inverts between populations. On the seen vintages M1 under-predicts payoff (0.01138 against 0.01536) and M2 over-predicts heavily (0.02831), with slopes 0.509 and 0.249. On the unseen vintages M1 OVER-predicts (0.01907 against 0.01122) and M2 under-predicts mildly (0.00842), with slopes 0.347 and 0.529. M2's calibration slope is better than M1's on the unseen population and worse on the seen population.

calendar_decomposition.reason: stability.calendar covers the seen-vintage evaluation population only. A per-year decomposition of the unseen-vintage population is not frozen and cannot be produced without scoring the prediction arrays.

hypotheses_for_the_reversal.hypothesis: Younger loans with different seasoning at entry
hypotheses_for_the_reversal.partial_support: Vintages 2018, 2020 and 2022 are structurally younger than 2006-2014. Not demonstrated as the cause.

A 2022-vintage facility cannot contribute risk intervals during 2020, so the unseen population is demonstrably less exposed to the 2020 calendar cell as a seasoned cohort. The exact calendar distribution of unseen-vintage intervals is not frozen, so the magnitude of this effect is not established.

hypotheses_for_the_reversal.hypothesis: Zero-reference cohort encoding for unrepresented vintages
hypotheses_for_the_reversal.partial_support: Frozen encoding rule is documented; its quantitative effect is not isolated.
The seen cohort is selected for non-prepayment through 2019; the unseen cohort is not. Consistent with the lower unseen payoff rate of 1.12% against 1.54%, but not demonstrated.

SA01 established that M2's pooled payoff AUC gain on the seen population is predominantly between-period. The much larger unseen payoff AUC gain of +0.185 may share that mechanism, but no stratified decomposition is available for this population.

primary_result: The sign reversal on the primary decision metric exists and applies to the unseen-vintage supplementary population comprising origination vintages 2018, 2020 and 2022, 17,352 facilities and 652,508 risk intervals, evaluated over the same 2019-01 to 2026-02 window.
study_level_justification: Option A fails because the primary metric reverses. Option B overstates: deterioration is not wholly confined to the seen-vintage population, since payoff Brier and default AUC still favour M1 on the unseen vintages, though payoff Brier deterioration is an order of magnitude smaller there (+0.000465 against +0.004698). Option D is wrong because both population results are frozen, internally consistent and reportable. The evidence shows transport behaviour that differs by population: severe joint-loss deterioration in the seasoned seen-vintage cohort, slight joint-loss improvement with persistent but much smaller cause-Brier deterioration in the younger unseen cohort.
status_reason: The reversal is verified directly from the frozen artifact and fully reported; only the per-year decomposition of this population is unavailable.
